patients.label: 72-year-old male with cervical and inguinal lymphadenopathy and classical Hodgkin lymphoma

identity_evidence.quote: We describe a case of a 72-year-old male with progressive bilateral cervical and inguinal lymphadenopathy

attribution_limitations: The abstract states Ann Arbor stage IIIB; the results paragraph and the discussion state Ann Arbor Stage II. The stage letter B in IIIB would normally relate to B symptoms, which the case presentation denies.

The introduction states the case shows B symptoms such as fever, weight loss and skin itch, whereas the case presentation, abstract and discussion state constitutional or B symptoms were absent. The introduction sentence names this case ("This case stands out") and its next sentence matches this patient's FNAC, so it is treated as a statement about this patient, not general background.
The results paragraph reports CECT nodes in the cervical, axillary, para-aortic and mesenteric regions, whereas the discussion says CT involvement was confined to cervical and inguinal lymph nodes.
The abstract and discussion describe bilateral cervical and inguinal lymphadenopathy, while the case presentation describes a right cervical and a left inguinal node.
Hepatosplenomegaly is reported on ultrasonography while the clinical examination found none; the sources describe different assessment methods.
The results paragraph describes a polymorphous inflammatory background, the discussion a fibrotic inflammatory background, and the abstract a polymorphous background.
The abstract says primary clinical and radiographic assessment favored an infectious or metastatic etiology, whereas the results paragraph says the CT raised suspicion for lymphoma.
The discussion says timely management can achieve meaningful remission as illustrated in this case, but the case reports chemotherapy initiated with interim PET-CT results awaited and no remission.
The case text says Figure 1 shows greyish-white lymphoid tissue, but the Figure 1 photograph shows a pale pink-tan fragment with a reddish-orange irregular area.
